title: Amendment – Board Policy – BP 3312 Contracts and Delegation of Authority
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment of Board Policy - Business and Noninstructional Operations - BP 3312 Contracts and Delegation of Authority, updating the Policy, if approved, to add the Chief Business Officer with delegated authority to enter into a Contract up to $50,000.00, in a Fiscal Year, cumulatively, with a vendor.
headline: Lets the Chief Business Officer sign vendor contracts up to $50,000 a year
summary: This updates Board Policy 3312 so the Chief Business Officer can enter into contracts with a single vendor without a separate board vote, up to $50,000 in total in a fiscal year. It changes who has signing authority; it does not spend money by itself.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, College and Career Access Pathways Act (CCAP) Agreement - AB 288 - District and Peralta Community College District
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, College and Career Access Pathways Act (CCAP) Agreement* - AB 288 - by and between the District and Peralta Community College District, for the latter to provide AB 288 pathway courses, as defined, to high school students of the District, is amended as specified in paragraphs 2 through 4 of the Amendment, providing for online/distance learning due to COVID-19 pandemic, naming Lucia Moritz as School District’s Representative and providing for increases in State allocation for Dual Enrollment and all Special Populations as specified.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Amends dual-enrollment agreement with Peralta Community College District for online learning
summary: This changes the existing College and Career Access Pathways Act (CCAP) agreement under which Peralta Community College District teaches college pathway courses to Oakland high school students. The amendment allows online and distance learning because of the COVID-19 pandemic, names the district's representative, and covers increases in state funding for dual enrollment and special populations. All other terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - Partnership - District and Roses in Concrete Charter School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding by and between the District and Roses in Concrete, a Charter School, defining a partnership “bringing the latter” into Howard Elementary School, a District school, commencing with a “Design Year” effective School Year 2020-21, pursuant to the terms and conditions thereof.
headline: Partners with Roses in Concrete charter school to bring it into Howard Elementary
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) sets up a partnership in which Roses in Concrete, a charter school, will operate at Howard Elementary School, a District school. It starts with a "Design Year" in School Year 2020-21. The text does not state a dollar amount.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Collective Bargaining Agreement Between the District and United Administrators of Oakland Schools (UAOS)
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Tentative Agreement, as Agreement Between District and United Administrators of Oakland Schools (UAOS), representing Certificated and Classified Administrators, for the period July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022, which includes a 5% on-going salary increase for unit non-retirees effective July 1, 2020, a 5% salary increase effective January 1, 2020 for unit employees at time of UAOS ratification who retire on or before June 30, 2020 and bonuses, as described therein.
headline: Approves 3-year contract with the school administrators' union, with 5% raises
summary: This adopts a tentative agreement with United Administrators of Oakland Schools (UAOS), the union for certificated and classified administrators, covering July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022. It includes a 5% ongoing raise starting July 1, 2020 for employees who are not retiring, a 5% raise effective January 1, 2020 for those who retire on or before June 30, 2020, and bonuses described in the agreement. The text gives no dollar totals.
pulled_from_consent: Taken off the consent vote, then approved on a later consent report on August 1.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
